Routing evidence:
- Option C (regional office) was accepted for south-region claims (small and large) and a south-region large shipment.
- Option C was rejected for all observed east-region requests (small invoice, small/large refund).
- Option C was also rejected for south-region large refunds.
- Requester wording, submitter department, size, and paperwork/status notes did not reliably determine validity.
- Do not default to C merely because the note mentions a regional office; the explicit request attributes matter.
- For future decisions, treat C as likely suitable for south claims/shipments, but not south refunds or observed east requests. More examples are needed to infer the correct choices for A, B, and D.

Routing evidence:
- Option C (regional office) was accepted for south-region claims (small and large) and south-region large shipments.
- C was rejected for all observed east-region requests (small invoice, small/large refund, large claim) and for south-region large refunds.
- Option A (standard queue) was accepted for a north-region small invoice, an east-region small refund, and a north-region large refund.
- A was rejected for north-region small refunds (two cases), a north-region small claim, an east-region small shipment, and an east-region large claim.
- Requester wording, submitter department, size, and paperwork/status notes—including regional-office references—do not reliably determine validity.
- Do not default to C based on regional-office wording. C currently appears more plausible for south claims/shipments, but not south refunds or observed east requests.
- A has some valid cases across north/east, but no stable rule yet; do not infer validity from region, type, or size alone.
- More examples are needed to identify rules for A, B, and D.

Routing evidence:
- C is consistently valid for south-region shipments (small and large) and south-region claims (small and large). It is invalid for observed south refunds and the south large invoice.
- B is valid for the east small shipment and north large shipment. B was rejected for the north large claim. More B examples are needed.
- A is valid for a north small invoice, east small refund, and north large refund. It is invalid for north small refunds (two cases), north small claim, east small shipment, east large claim, and north large shipment.
- D was rejected for a north small refund; no positive D evidence exists.
- Region, request type, size, requester wording, submitter department, and paperwork/status notes do not independently explain validity. Regional-office wording is not sufficient to select C.
- Current strongest pattern: C for south shipments; A or B may apply to some north/east requests, but do not infer from region, type, or size alone.
- Treat each route/type/region combination as uncertain until supported by examples; continue collecting evidence, especially for B and D and unobserved combinations.

Routing evidence:
- C has positive evidence for south small/large shipments and south small/large claims in earlier cases, but was rejected for a new south large claim. C is also invalid for observed south refunds and the south large invoice. Do not treat C as universally valid for south requests.
- B is valid for the east small shipment and north large shipment in earlier cases, but was rejected for a north large claim, north small shipment, south large invoice, east large shipment, south small refund, and north large shipment. B is now especially unreliable.
- A is valid for a north small invoice, east small refund, and north large refund. It was rejected for two north small refunds, north small claim, east small shipment, east large claim, north large shipment, east small claim, and north large claim. The new east small refund acceptance confirms one positive A case; the requester wording differs, so wording is not enough to generalize.
- D has no positive evidence; it was rejected for a north small refund.
- Regional office wording, requester wording, submitter department, paperwork format, urgency, and status notes have not independently explained validity.
- Recent negatives: east small claim=A; north small shipment=B; south small refund=A and B; south large claim=C; south large invoice=B; east large shipment=B; north large claim=A; north large shipment=B.
- Treat every combination as uncertain. Do not infer routing from region, request type, size, or incidental wording alone. Continue collecting evidence, prioritizing D and repeated combinations with conflicting outcomes.

Routing evidence:
- Every combination remains uncertain; region, request type, size, wording, department, paperwork, urgency, and status notes do not independently determine routing.
- A: positive for north small invoice, east small refund, and north large refund. Rejected for north small refunds, north small claim, east small shipment, east large claim, east small claim, north large claim, and north large refund (new step 41). Treat A as unreliable even on previously positive combinations.
- B: positive for east small shipment and north large shipment in earlier cases, but rejected for north large claim, north small shipment, south large invoice, east large shipment, south small refund, and east small shipment (step 43). Especially unreliable.
- C: positive for south small/large shipments and south small/large claims in earlier cases, plus south large shipment (step 46); rejected for south large claim. Not universally valid.
- D: previously had no positive evidence, but is now valid for north small shipment (step 45). Rejected for north small refund, east small claim (step 40), north small claim, north large invoice, south large claim, large invoice east, and large refund north. Do not generalize the new positive.
- New negatives: north large refund=A; east large invoice=D; east small shipment=B; north small claim=D; north large invoice=D; south large claim=D.
- Repeated combinations can conflict: east small shipment has both B-positive earlier and B-negative recently; north small shipment has B-negative and D-positive. Continue collecting evidence, prioritizing D and conflicting/repeated combinations.

Routing evidence:
- No feature (region, request type, size, wording, department, paperwork, urgency, or status) independently determines routing. Do not generalize from one combination.
- A: positive for north small invoice, east small refund, north large refund (earlier), and south small invoice (step 57). Rejected for north small refunds, north small/large claims, east small/large invoices, east small shipment, east/south? large claims, and north large refund (step 41). Treat as unreliable.
- B: earlier positive for east/north large shipment and east small shipment, but rejected for north large claim, north small shipment, south large invoice, east large shipment, south small refund, and east small shipment (step 43). Especially unreliable.
- C: earlier positive for south small/large shipments and claims, but rejected for south large claim, north large claim (step 50), east small claim (step 51), south large refund (step 55), north small refund (step 56), south large invoice (step 58), and north small claim (step 59). Not universal.
- D: positive for north small shipment (step 45). Rejected for north small refund, east small claim, north small claim, north large invoice, south large claim, east large invoice (step 52), east large shipment (step 54), and north large refund. Do not generalize the positive.
- Recent negatives: east large invoice=A (steps 52–53), east large shipment=D, south large refund=C, north small refund=C, south large invoice=C, north small claim=C.
- Repeated combinations can conflict: east small shipment has B-positive and B-negative; north small shipment has B-negative and D-positive. Prioritize recent evidence but continue collecting examples; confidence remains low.
